messages.author: 0714839561195f1a
messages.subject: Error Referring to Group Balance
parts:
Hi Mike,

Could you please give me some ideas for my error below?

I'm trying to run a between-groups ANOVA; there are two groups,
distinguished by the value 0 or 1 in the 'level' variable. (I suppose I
should have used the variable name 'group' rather than 'level'.) Level 0
has 550 observations, and level 1 has 60 observations. So they are very
very unbalanced... but even when I try using "type=1", I receive the
same error. Further, the error refers to a within factor, which I'm not
using.

The two groups are "instructors" and "students" -- so it's very
unbalanced because for every instructor I have more than ten students.
If I really do have to balance the groups, I'll have to think of how to
do so!

Thanks for any suggestions,
Dan

> ezANOVA (df, .(dv), .(user), between=.(level), observed=.(level))
Warning: Data is unbalanced (unequal N per group). Make sure you
specified a well-considered value for the type argument to ezANOVA().
Error in names(x) <- value :
'names' attribute [8] must be the same length as the vector [7]
Error in ezANOVA_main(data = data, dv = dv, wid = wid, within = within, :
The car::Anova() function used to compute results and assumption
tests seems t
o have failed. Most commonly this is because you have too few subjects
relative
to the number of cells in the within-Ss design. It is possible that
trying the ANOVA again with "type=1" may yield results (but definitely
no assumption tests).

Hi Dan,

I'm really sorry for not responding earlier. Unfortunately you've
encountered one of the bigger bugs in ez v3.0
(https://github.com/mike-lawrence/ez/issues#issue/1). I'm hoping to
push out a big-ish update in the next couple of days, but in the
meantime you should be able to source the attached file after loading
ez to get the fix the problem you encountered. (note however that this
version of the code does not fix this issue:
https://github.com/mike-lawrence/ez/issues#issue/3)

Mike
